title: Personal Credit Cards: Standing of the Checking Account That Funds Autopay
content:
An automatic payment on Personal Credit Cards is debited from the checking account the card names as its paying account. Whether the bank, rather than the cardholder, is answerable for a debit that was never taken turns in part on that checking account: its ownership, its status, and whether it stood below zero on the due date.

## Requirements on the named checking account

- It is a Piedmont Crescent Bank checking account belonging to the cardholder.
- Its status on the bank's checking records is active. An account that is dormant, restricted, closed or in any other status does not meet this, and neither does a named account the bank's records do not hold.
- It was not overdrawn on the payment due date. The checking record carries the date on which the account's current negative stretch began; the account counts as funded on the due date when that negative-since date is blank or falls after the payment due date.

## Input, judgement, output (hypothetical dates, due date 18 June)

| Status of the named account | Negative-since date | Meets the requirements |
|---|---|---|
| active | blank | yes |
| active | 21 June | yes, it went negative only after the due date |
| active | 18 June | no, it was already negative on the due date |
| active | 2 June | no |
| dormant | blank | no |

## Points of judgement

- A negative-since date that falls on the due date itself means the account was overdrawn that day.
- An account that is overdrawn today but whose negative stretch began after the due date was still funded on the due date.
